entries.title: Convert the user prompt to a goal
entries.summary: Produce a concise execution goal that preserves the requested end state, scope, constraints, and explicit exclusions without adding process requirements.
instructions: Treat the user prompt as authoritative source material.
State what must be accomplished, not a plan for accomplishing it.
Preserve material scope limits, required outputs, and explicit exclusions.
Do not add verification, planning, research, or prerequisites unless the prompt itself makes them part of the requested end state.
Return only the goal in the required response shape.

entries.title: Convert the goal to knowledge-base queries
entries.summary: Translate the current goal into concise retrieval language likely to surface useful execution knowledge from the execution KB.
instructions: Write queries for knowledge that would help accomplish the goal; do not solve the goal in this step.
Use concrete verbs, objects, execution situations, capabilities, and constraints that are likely to occur in KB retrieval fields.
Use more than one query when materially different execution knowledge may be needed.
Do not invent KB identifiers.
Return only the query list in the required response shape.

entries.title: Select useful retrieved KB topics
entries.summary: Choose the retrieved KB records whose full contents should be supplied as task context for the next phase.
instructions: Select by semantic usefulness to the stated goal, not merely lexical similarity.
A topic is a retrieved KB record represented by its canonical record ID, type, and summary.
Select every candidate that may materially inform execution; selection is not a requirement to use every selected record later.
Do not invent or rewrite topic IDs.
Return only IDs present in the supplied candidate list.

entries.title: Synthesize the instruction that will solve the goal
entries.summary: Given the execution goal and the selected full KB records, construct the complete instruction that a model should follow to solve the goal under that supplied knowledge and produce the required executable contract.
instructions: Treat the goal as the required end state and the selected KB records as the operative execution context.
Construct an instruction for solving the goal; do not solve the goal in this step.
The instruction must tell the next model step to use the supplied goal and KB context to determine the concrete execution needed.
The instruction must require a complete executable Python script, not a plan or explanation.
The instruction must require the Python script to write exactly one JSON object to stdout on successful completion and reserve stderr for diagnostics.
The instruction must require a JSON Schema describing that successful model-facing result.
Do not add requirements that are not supported by the goal or supplied KB context.
Return only the synthesized instruction in the required response shape.

entries.title: Apply the synthesized instruction
entries.summary: Execute the synthesized solver instruction semantically using the same goal and selected full KB records, and return the executable contract it calls for.
instructions: Follow the supplied solver instruction as the immediate task instruction.
Use the supplied goal and selected full KB records as its grounding context.
Produce the complete executable Python source as execution_script; do not wrap source in Markdown fences.
The generated Python must write exactly one JSON object to stdout on successful completion and use stderr only for diagnostics or errors.
Produce return_schema as the JSON Schema for that one successful model-facing stdout object.
The transaction result contains exactly execution_script and return_schema.
Choose the transition separately as execute, revise, or exit.
